home_presentation: Welcome! My name is Adrien, I'm 21 years old, and I'm passionate about space and network programming in the video game industry. I'm particularly interested in low-level network programming and the technical challenges it involves. I also enjoy everything surrounding this field, including infrastructure management, automation, and performance optimization.
gameProjects_description_tme: Multiplatform TCP netcode (Windows and POSIX), written in C++17. This is my first netcode project. It allowed me to take my first steps in network programming and learn about the low-level mechanisms used in multiplayer games.
gameProjects_description_suna: Competitive FPS in the style of Counter-Strike. You play as either the Natives or the Corporates. One team’s objective is to plant the Harvester, while the opposing team must prevent it from being planted or defuse it if it has already been deployed.
gameProjects_description_fairy_fields: Mobile farming game with a magical twist. Build your farm to grow plants and transform them into potions to fulfill the villagers requests. You can also trade by buying and selling items with other players.
gameProjects_description_shattered_soul: In this 2D top-down roguelike, you play as a knightess whose soul ascends toward Divinity upon death. To contain this newfound power, she must defeat a god and claim her body as a vessel.
gameProjects_description_solar_storm: In this board game, you must work together as a team to escape your ship, which is drifting straight into a solar storm. To survive, you’ll need to collect metal to build shuttles, while also producing food and water. But beware if you run out of either, you’ll be forced to say goodbye to one of your own.
gameProjects_description_land_of_hope: In this turn-based tactical game, your objective is to conquer the Bad Lands. You’ll begin by choosing your hero and soldiers, then move your troops across a tactical map, with combat inspired by Slay the Spire.
project_description_Travelers_Netcode: Travelers-Netcode is a multiplatform netcode (Windows and POSIX), developed in C++17. This is my first netcode project. It allowed me to take my first steps in network programming and explore the low-level mechanisms used in multiplayer games.
project_role_description_Travelers_Netco: As the lead developer of this solo project, I am responsible for the entire development cycle: from designing the cross-platform network architecture to implementing the C++ code, through feature testing and performance optimization. My approach consists of progressively validating each concept on simple prototypes before integrating them into more complex and demonstrable samples.
project_role_responsibility_Travelers_Ne: Built a cross-platform (Windows / Linux) TCP socket communication layer
Designed a message system with automatic serialization and deserialization of custom message types
Implemented a client-server architecture using a custom ECS to synchronize entities and their components
Created a component system where components are automatically serialized, deserialized and replicated between clients and server
Implemented a snapshot system to synchronize entities and their linked network components between server and clients
project_feature_desc_Travelers_Netcode_0: Basic implementation of TCP and UDP sockets (the UDP code is present but has never been used)

Serialization and deserialization system using macros to enable the creation of custom messages that are automatically serialized for transmission over the network and deserialized on the receiving end.

I used an ECS that I developed myself (Travelers-ECS). It allows the netcode to handle network entities and components that are automatically synchronized between the server and the different clients. The network components use a macro system that allows custom network components to be created while automating their serialization and deserialization

This system automatically synchronizes all entities and their network components. Users only need to create a network entity for it to be automatically replicated. Similarly, when a network component is added to or removed from an entity, it is automatically replicated or removed across all clients. Network components are then kept up to date according to a customizable tick rate

A wrapper that provides access to the entire netcode system, including server and client creation, client-to-server connections, configuration of various parameters (such as the snapshot tick rate), creation and management of network entities and components, and handling of various events. The main goal is to keep the entire ECS system encapsulated within the netcode, so users are not required to use an ECS in their own projects
project_learnings_desc_Travelers_Netcode: This project has already allowed me to deepen my understanding of the many aspects of network development and its fundamental constraints. I continue to learn and progressively integrate this new knowledge into this netcode.
project_description_suna_1: Suna is a competitive multiplayer first-person shooter inspired by Counter-Strike. In this game, two teams face off: the Corpos and the Natives.
project_description_suna_2: As a Corpo, you play as a combat robot with the objective of planting an extractor or eliminating the entire enemy team. As a Native, you are one of the planet's inhabitants, and your mission is to protect your resources by preventing the Corpos from planting the extractor or annihilating their team.
project_role_description_suna: As a network and gameplay programmer, I was responsible for implementing the foundation of the shooting system, hit detection and damage management, as well as creating a hybrid animation system combining Unity's ECS and its GameObject-based animation system. I also integrated animations and ensured proper player replication (movements, animations, shots, damage), while ensuring the game remains playable despite considerable ping.
project_role_responsibility_suna_02: Implementation of the networked shooting system foundation.
project_role_responsibility_suna_03: Handling of FPS and TPS models through GameObjects, integrated with ECS for operations such as creation, destruction, movement, rotation, and replication.
project_role_responsibility_suna_04: Hit detection and damage management related to player shooting.
project_role_responsibility_suna_05: Implementation of a networked hybrid animation system between Unity's ECS and the GameObject-based animation system.
project_role_responsibility_suna_07: FPS camera system and spectator mode.
project_role_responsibility_suna_08: Replication of player movements, animations, and shooting.
project_feature_desc_suna_01: The network architecture is composed of multiple clients and a separate server, with centralized authority ensured by the server.
project_feature_desc_suna_02: Automatically gathers players and forms teams to quickly launch a match.
project_feature_desc_suna_03: Ensures proper replication and consistency of movements, animations, and player actions, whether with low or high ping.
project_feature_desc_suna_04: Implements the entire match flow: buy phase, extractor placement and defusal, win/loss management, and transitions between different phases.
project_feature_desc_suna_05: Manages the game's economy: money allocation based on actions, equipment purchases at the start of rounds, and rewards or penalties based on results.
project_challenge_desc_suna_01: For this project, we used Unity DOTS, which replaces Unity's traditional GameObject system with an entity-based system (ECS). Since Unity DOTS is still a technology in development, it doesn't have an integrated animation system. One of my responsibilities was therefore to create a hybrid system allowing the connection between ECS, which manages entity values and states, and Unity's traditional GameObject-based animation system. All while ensuring proper replication and network synchronization.
project_challenge_solution_suna_01_desc: I developed a hybrid system that uses dynamic buffers to store animation parameters (float, int, bool, trigger) as ECS components with network synchronization via GhostComponent. On the server, a system collects state changes and stores them in these buffers, while another system applies them to the traditional Unity Animator. On the client, the system automatically receives replicated data and updates animations locally. This architecture allows a clear separation between ECS logic and rendering, while ensuring smooth animation synchronization across all connected players.
project_learnings_desc_suna: This project was a wonderful experience for me, allowing me to improve my skills, acquire new ones, and confirm my desire to specialize in network programming. I also had the opportunity to work with a great team to deliver an ambitious project within a tight deadline.
project_learning_suna_01: Programming a networked multiplayer game with prediction, replication, synchronization, and server-side authority.
project_learning_suna_02: Discover and learn ECS (Entity Component System) programming.
project_learning_suna_03: Improvement of my teamwork and communication skills.
project_learning_suna_04: Ability to produce functional and optimized code, even under tight deadlines.
